Love Field to Greenville: matching Dallas aerospace NDT work to NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A

Dallas itself has no single giant aircraft plant; it has a wide aviation economy spread across several counties. The Dallas Regional Chamber counts hundreds of aviation and aerospace companies in North Texas. Southwest Airlines is headquartered in Dallas and runs large maintenance operations at Love Field. Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control is based in Grand Prairie. L3Harris modifies aircraft at a large site in Greenville, east of the city, and Spirit AeroSystems' Dallas operations joined Boeing when that acquisition closed in December 2025. Around them sit component repair shops, avionics makers and processors that machine, plate and heat-treat parts. The same metro runs pipelines, power plants and steel fabrication on ASME, API and AWS codes, so the standard printed on a Dallas technician's certification can change with each job.

Which document each kind of Dallas employer usually works to

Employer around DallasPersonnel standard you will usually meetWhere it comes from
Airline hangar or Part 145 repair station at Love Field or DFWThe document its maintenance or repair station manual names: NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 or SNT-TC-1AFAA AC 65-31B lists all three as acceptable; the FAA itself certifies no NDT personnel
Aircraft modification lineOften NAS 410, when the military or prime customer invokes itThe contract and the engineering orders issued under it
Processor or machine shop supplying missile or aerostructure programsNAS 410, or EN 4179 on European ordersThe purchase-order quality clause, flowed down to each sub-tier that tests hardware
Nadcap-accredited NDT houseNAS 410 under a Responsible Level 3 designated in writingAC7114 audits that trace each certification back to its evidence
Pipeline, plant or structural steel contractorSNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 where a code names it, as Section XI outage work at Comanche Peak doesASME, API 1104 and AWS D1.1, adopted through the written practice

Changing employers in the Metroplex

A Dallas technician might spend three years on a Love Field hangar floor, two on a Greenville modification line and the next stretch in a Grand Prairie component shop. Each move restarts certification, because neither scheme issues a portable card. What travels is evidence: course outlines with recorded hours, an experience log signed method by method, every examination record marked with the standard it was taken under, and current eye-test results. The new employer's RL3 decides what to credit. An SNT-TC-1A certification helps that review, but it never meets a NAS 410 requirement by itself, and the usual gap is formal penetrant and magnetic particle training, where NAS 410 asks for more than SNT-TC-1A recommends. Keep copies of everything; a company that closes or merges does not always forward old files.

For Dallas shops answering a NAS 410 clause

Plenty of Dallas companies run a hangar at one airport and a component shop in an industrial park. One written practice can cover both sites, but each site's technique sheets and examination banks have to sit under it, not beside it. Print the governing standard and revision on every certification, move NAS 410 work to Revision 6, released in December 2025, when your customers call for it, and expect Nadcap or customer auditors to walk from a signed report back to the inspector's file. Atlantis prepares and reviews that evidence through NAS 410 audit documentation for Dallas suppliers and repair stations, and your RL3 approves it. Background on the RL3 role is in NAS 410 explained.

What Atlantis covers in Dallas

Atlantis training is based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory, Q&A with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), the Practical NDT simulator, and the practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Dallas. Our ASNT Level III consulting for aerospace and aviation covers written practices aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, procedures, Level I and II examinations and outside agency Level III services in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Dallas-area employers. A Dallas aerospace employer's RL3 is the person who decides whether outside training counts toward its NAS 410 certifications, so ask before you enroll. For detail, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A and see eddy current testing in aviation and penetrant testing training.
